title: Querying: files, owners, versions
summary: List a package's files, find which package owns a file, list what is installed, and compare versions like dpkg does.

steps.title: Who owns what
body: | Question | Debian | RHEL / SUSE | Arch | Alpine |
| files in an installed package | `dpkg -L nginx` | `rpm -ql nginx` | `pacman -Ql nginx` | `apk info -L nginx` |
| which package owns this file? | `dpkg -S /usr/sbin/nginx` | `rpm -qf /usr/sbin/nginx` | `pacman -Qo /usr/sbin/nginx` | `apk info --who-owns /usr/sbin/nginx` |
| which package **would** provide it? | `apt-file search bin/dig` | `dnf provides '*/bin/dig'` | `pacman -F dig` | `apk search cmd:dig` |
| list installed | `apt list --installed`, `dpkg -l` | `rpm -qa`, `dnf list installed` | `pacman -Q` | `apk info -v` |
The "would provide" column answers the everyday question *"`dig: command not found`, what do I install?"* (Debian: `dnsutils` / `bind9-dnsutils`; RHEL: `bind-utils`).

steps.prompt: Match the question to the Debian command.
Same question, other families. Which question does each command answer?

steps.title: Reading the listings
body: ```text
$ apt list --installed
Listing... Done
bash/noble,now 5.2.21-2ubuntu4 amd64 [installed]
curl/noble-updates,now 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.4 amd64 [installed,automatic]
$ rpm -qa
python3-libs-3.9.18-3.el9.x86_64

apt: `name/suites version arch [flags]`. rpm: `name-version-release.arch`, where the **name may contain dashes**, so you split from the right: the last `.` gives the arch, the last `-` the release, the one before it the version.

checks.fail: Count the installed packages: `dpkg -l | grep -c '^ii'` or `apt list --installed 2>/dev/null | grep -c installed`.

checks.name: biggest.txt
checks.fail: The list does not match. `dpkg-query -W -f='${Installed-Size}\t${Package}\n' | sort -rn | head -n5`.

hints: `dpkg -S PATH` answers "who owns this file"; `dpkg -L PACKAGE` the reverse.
`dpkg-query -W -f='${Version}' curl > ~/answers/curl-version.txt`. `-f` takes any control field, like `${Installed-Size}` or `${Status}`.
explain: These are the questions behind most "why is the image so big?" and "which version are we really running?" tickets.
`apt list --installed` is friendlier to read but warns that its output is not stable for scripts; `dpkg-query -W -f` is
the scriptable one. On RPM systems: `rpm -qf PATH`, `rpm -q --qf '%{VERSION}-%{RELEASE}' curl`, `rpm -qa | wc -l`.

steps.title: Comparing versions
body: Is `1.10` newer than `1.9`? As strings no, as versions yes. Debian's rules (dpkg), close to rpm's:
1. A version is `[epoch:]upstream[-revision]`. A higher **epoch** always wins: `1:0.9` > `2.0`.
2. Compare upstream, then revision, piece by piece, alternating a **non-digit** run and a **digit** run.
3. Digit runs compare as numbers: `10` > `9`.
4. Non-digit runs compare character by character where `~` sorts **before everything, even the end of the string**, then the end of the string, then letters, then other symbols.
So `1.0~rc1` < `1.0` < `1.0a` < `1.0+b1`. That `~` rule is why pre-releases are packaged as `2.0~beta1`. Check with `dpkg --compare-versions 1.0~rc1 lt 1.0 && echo yes`.

steps.prompt: Is the left version older than the right one?

steps.title: Let dpkg compare versions
prompt: Never compare package versions as text or as numbers: `1.2.10` is newer than `1.2.9`, `1.2~rc1` is **older** than `1.2`,
and an epoch (`2:`) beats everything after it. `dpkg --compare-versions A gt B` knows every rule and answers with its
`~/versions.txt` has two versions per line. Write `~/answers/newer.txt`: for each line, in order, the **newer** of the
two (none of the pairs are equal). Use `dpkg --compare-versions` in a loop.

checks.name: newer.txt picks the newer version on every line
checks.cmd: diff ~/answers/newer.txt <(while read -r a b; do if dpkg --compare-versions "$a" gt "$b"; then echo "$a"; else echo "$b"; fi; done < ~/versions.txt)
checks.fail: Some lines are wrong (diff below: `<` yours, `>` what dpkg says). Let `dpkg --compare-versions` decide each pair.

hints: `dpkg --compare-versions 1.2~rc1 lt 1.2 && echo yes` prints `yes`. The operators are `lt le eq ne ge gt`.
Read two words per line: `while read -r a b; do ...; done < ~/versions.txt`.
Inside: `if dpkg --compare-versions "$a" gt "$b"; then echo "$a"; else echo "$b"; fi`, and redirect the whole loop into the answer file.
solution: while read -r a b; do if dpkg --compare-versions "$a" gt "$b"; then echo "$a"; else echo "$b"; fi; done < ~/versions.txt > ~/answers/newer.txt
explain: The `~` rule is why Debian can ship `2.0~beta2` before `2.0` and still upgrade cleanly, and the epoch is how a
maintainer recovers from a version scheme that went backwards. Ubuntu's `1.0-1ubuntu0.1` is newer than Debian's
`1.0-1`, which is how its security fixes win. On RPM systems, `rpmdev-vercmp` does the same job.
